children.value: During the task the cursor position was recorded together with the button states and the task phase. The nets are placed by clicking on the slots of the circle, so the recording shows, for every net (token), the movement that led to it, the order in which the nets were placed, and where the cursor rested before the placement phase began. This chapter describes the extraction of these measures and their relation to the instruction condition, the questionnaire scores, the placement strategies and the parameters of the latent-state model.

The cursor is sampled every 33–50 ms. Positions are in task units; the slots lie on a circle of radius 8 around the centre. Each trial has an anticipation phase, a placement phase and an inter-stimulus interval. At the onset of the placement phase the cursor is reset to the centre, so the movement to the first token starts at the centre on every trial.
is a left-button press during the placement phase at a radius between 5 and 11; its location is the angle of the press. Token 1 starts at the onset of the placement phase, token
of the result file. Per participant there are 171–188 trials and 1,076–1,228 tokens (median 1,161).

In 87 % of the trials (participant range 63–100 %) every slot that holds a net in the result file is within one slot of a press. The remaining trials contain nets that were placed on a neighbouring slot of the press (stacked nets).

The movement from the token’s start to its press is time-normalised to 101 points and compared with the direct path between start and press:
maximum absolute perpendicular deviation from the direct path (signed)
signed area between trajectory and direct path (shoelace area of the trajectory closed by the direct path); absolute version: absolute deviation integrated over the progress along the path
reversals of the movement along the direct path (steps below 0.1 units ignored), and the time of the first one
time until the cursor has moved 0.3 units
time from placement onset to the press of token 1
Each colour cue has two target directions, its two latent states. On every trial,
is the target direction of the trial,
the other target direction of the cue, and
the direction 120° from both. Token 1 is classified as at the current state, the other state or the third direction (the nearest of the three within 45°), or elsewhere.

When token 1 goes to the current state and the other state receives no token in the trial, the deviation of the token-1 trajectory toward the other state measures how strongly the unchosen alternative competes for the response (Freeman & Ambady, 2010): maximum deviation toward the other state (0 if none), and the signed area toward it.

Shannon entropy (bits) of the cursor’s angular position in 32 sectors of the circle, weighted by the time spent at each sample, separately for the anticipation phase and the placement phase. Samples within radius 3 of the centre are left out. 0 means the cursor stays in one sector, 5 that it spends equal time in all sectors. In the anticipation phase the cursor stays near the centre on 38 % of the trials, which then have no anticipation entropy.
Angle and radius of the cursor at the end of the anticipation phase, before the reset.

the direction of the displaced attack. Events at which the participant’s own nets were already within 45° of the displaced attack are left out (1,857 event placements). Token 1 is classified as at old or new (the nearer within 45°) or elsewhere. When the anticipation position lies at old or new (within 45°), token 1 goes to the same location in 85 % (new) and 65 % (old) of the placements.

The participant means of the trajectory and entropy measures are stable within the session: the split-half reliability (odd vs even trials, Spearman–Brown corrected) is .89 to .99 for token 1 at the current and at the other state, pull, curvature, direction changes, response time and spatial entropy (

). The share of transitions with token 1 at the previous state rests on eight transitions per participant and has a reliability of .46 (95 % CI .23–.63), so single participants’ values of this measure are imprecise even though the group association with the scores is strong.

shows the deviation of the movement to token 1 toward the unchosen other state for each participant, ordered by STICSA trait within the condition. Without instructions, the deviation of higher scorers is larger over the middle of the movement (+0.050 per SD, p = .005); with partial and full instructions, the deviation is larger in most participants regardless of the score, and the slopes are near zero (Partial −0.005, p = .89; Full −0.005, p = .83). The pattern is carried by many participants with a moderate pull rather than by a few extreme ones.

On the first trial of a new episode, token 1 goes to the previous state in a median of 75 % (None), 88 % (Partial) and 88 % (Full) of the eight transitions. One and two trials later, the share at the old location falls to about 30 % and 15 %, with large differences between participants (
). Within the conditions, the upper third of STICSA trait starts from a higher share at t0 in None and Partial; from t+1 on, the thirds of the score do not differ systematically.
